doc.title: Ralph Humphrey interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 11, 2003

title: Ron Carter, Herbie Hancock and Tony Williams rhythm section
summary: They discuss how rarely Carter, Hancock and Williams lost each other and Carter's role as go-between.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Sometimes I wish I could have read the minds of like Ron Carter and — like we think that they had this tremendous rapport going and sometimes you wonder like were they lost at all?

You know when I listen to the records with Herbie and Ron and Tony, they rarely lost one another. I mean yeah there are a couple of times when the beat got turned around and whatnot but it was so incidental and Ron was so good at reading Tony and laying down the — pinning down, acting as the go-between between Herbie and Tony. Because Herbie and Tony were back and forth with each other constantly you know. And Ron just knew what to do. So I have so much respect for that position in the band. The bass player is so key.
